Additional data point: **Mac mini (Mid 2012), Intel i7-3720QM (Ivy Bridge), macOS 14.4.1 Sonoma**.

The `darwin-x64-baseline` binary from v1.2.15 **also crashes with SIGILL** (exit code 132), same as the standard `darwin-x64` build.

This is because Bun has no macOS x64-baseline build — only Linux and Windows get baseline binaries that drop the AVX2 requirement (ref: oven-sh/bun#17912). So the "baseline" designation on macOS is currently ineffective; the embedded Bun runtime still targets Haswell (AVX2).

```
$ /tmp/oc-baseline/opencode version
zsh: illegal hardware instruction  /tmp/oc-baseline/opencode
$ echo $?
132
```

CPU features confirm AVX1 present, AVX2 absent:
```
machdep.cpu.brand_string: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-3720QM CPU @ 2.60GHz
machdep.cpu.features: ... AVX1.0 ...
machdep.cpu.leaf7_features: SMEP ERMS  (no AVX2)
```

Related issue I created (before finding this one): #15486

## Finding: separate clones were colliding

While fixing #14082 (worktrees splitting project IDs), we noticed another scenario: *two separate clones* of the same git repo can end up sharing a project identity if the ID is derived from repo history (eg. root commit). In the UI this shows up as selecting one project selecting both.

## Fix

- Git project identity is now a per-clone UUID cached in the git *common* dir: `<git-common-dir>/opencode`.
  - Worktrees share the same common dir → same project id
  - Separate clones have different common dirs → different project id
- Legacy root-commit IDs (40-hex) are migrated in `Project.repairAll()` (DB backup + migrate Project/Session/Permission rows).
- `Project.fromDirectory()` does **not** perform DB repairs/migrations.
